result.topic_en: Formula-only calculations for one-dimensional gas motion (air waves): characteristic-type variables p, q, the relations x'_1 = 2a(p+q), log ρ_1 = 2(p−q), and the resulting linear first-order equations for t and x in terms of p and q, including an exponential/trigonometric (imaginary) variant.
result.transcription:
$\frac{\partial x}{\partial p}dp+\frac{\partial x}{\partial q}dq = \frac{\partial x}{\partial t}\left(\frac{\partial t}{\partial p}dp+\frac{\partial t}{\partial q}.dq\right)$ \qquad $\overline{p+q}\,i = \sin\overline{p-q}\,i$
[-$\frac{\partial p}{\partial \ldots}$-] $\frac{\partial x}{\partial t} = x_1'+a\sqrt{\frac{\varrho_2}{\varrho_1}} = x_2'+a\sqrt{\frac{\varrho_1}{\varrho_2}}$ \qquad $\frac{\partial x}{\partial t} = a\,e^{p-q} = a\left(2(p+q)+e^{q-p}\right)$
[-$2at$-] [-$\frac{1}{\ldots}$-] $x_1' = 2a(p+q)$ \quad $x_2'=0$
$\log\varrho_1 \cdot n \log\varrho_2 = 0$ [?] \qquad $2(p+q) = e^{p-q}-e^{q-p}$
$\log\varrho_1 = 2(p-q)$
[-$p+q$-] [-$e^{p-q}$-]
$(p+q)i = \sin(p-q)i$ \qquad $(dp+dq)i = \cos(p-q)i\;dp\,i - dq\,i$
$dp(\cos\overline{p-q}\,i-1) = dq(\cos(p-q)i+1)$
$\frac{\partial x}{\partial q} = 2a\left(p+q+\frac12\right)\frac{\partial t}{\partial q}$ \qquad [-$\ldots$-] $e^{p-q}-e^{q-p}-1$
$\frac{\partial x}{\partial p} = 2a\left(p+q-\frac12\right)\frac{\partial t}{\partial p}$.
$\frac{\partial t}{\partial p}dp\left(\frac{\partial x}{\partial t}-2a\left(p+q-\frac12\right)\right)+\frac{\partial t}{\partial q}\left(\frac{\partial x}{\partial t}-2a\left(p+q+\frac12\right)\right)dq=0$
$a\frac{(1+e^{q-p})}{(e^{q-p}-1)^2}$ \qquad $a(e^{q-p}-1)\frac{\cos(p-q)i+1}{(e^{q-p}+1)^2}$
[-$(1-2\alpha^2-\alpha^3)\partial$-]
$\frac{\partial t}{\partial p}(e^{q-p}-1)+\frac{\partial t}{\partial q}(e^{q-p}+1)=0$
$\frac{\partial x}{\partial p} = (1-\alpha-\alpha^2)\frac{a}{\alpha}\frac{\partial t}{\partial p}$ \quad $\frac{\partial x}{\partial q} = (1+\alpha-\alpha^2)\frac{\partial t}{\partial q}\frac{a}{\alpha}$
$\frac{\partial t}{\partial p}(\alpha-1)+\frac{\partial t}{\partial q}(\alpha+1)=0$ \quad $\frac{\partial x}{\partial p}(-1+2\alpha^2-\alpha^3)+(1-2\alpha^2\pm\alpha^3)\frac{\partial x}{\partial q}$
$=0$
